fidelity: F2a — Physics-Lumped Recompression Brayton Cycle with Thermal ODE
source: Dostal, Driscoll & Hejzlar (2004) MIT-ANP-TR-100; Ahn et al. (2015) Nucl. Eng. Technol. 47, 647-661; Span & Wagner (1996) J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 25, 1509-1596; Crespi et al. (2017) Appl. Energy 195, 152-183.

unit.name: 10 MWe Recompression sCO2 Brayton Cycle — Physics-Lumped State-Point Model

T_turb_in_K.note: Turbine inlet temperature (700 degC sCO2 design point); Dostal 2004

T_comp_in_K.note: Main compressor inlet (32 degC, just above CO2 critical 30.98 degC) — near-critical operation is the key sCO2 advantage

P_high_Pa.note: High-side pressure (~25 MPa typical sCO2); Ahn 2015

P_low_Pa.note: Low-side / compressor inlet pressure (above critical 7.377 MPa)

eta_comp.note: Isentropic efficiency, main + recompression compressor; Dostal 2004

recompression_fraction.note: Fraction of flow routed to recompression compressor (bypasses precooler); Dostal 2004 optimum ~0.3-0.4

mdot.note: CO2 mass flow rate for ~10 MWe net

T_crit_K.note: CO2 critical temperature (30.98 degC); Span & Wagner 1996

cp_ideal.note: CO2 ideal-gas cp at ~700 degC (high-T limit, weak real-gas effect)

gamma_ideal.note: CO2 ratio of specific heats (high-T, near ideal)

m_thermal.note: Lumped metal thermal mass of heater/turbine hot section

UA_hot.note: Heater-side overall conductance (heat source to metal)
